extracted.intended_audience: PR professionals and communicators who send press releases / anyone pitching journalists
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for crafting and timing press releases so journalists will open, consider, and cover them; covers initial triage, quick-content expectations, editorial checks, and factors that increase or decrease coverage likelihood.

rubrics_metrics.name: 4-Second Filter
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists give each release roughly 4 seconds before deciding to read or delete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decision is made on sender name (known source vs. unknown); subject line clarity; time of arrival (during deadline = delete); and whether the news affects their beat. Make these elements immediately obvious to survive the initial triage.

rubrics_metrics.name: 30-Second Filter
rubrics_metrics.description: If they open the release, reporters spend ~30 seconds scanning the content to decide whether to pursue it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must quickly show: a headline that tells the actual news; a lede paragraph with the 5 W's (who, what, when, where, why); a quote on the first page (signals a real source); spokesperson contact in the standard place; and multimedia available. These elements should be immediately accessible on first scan.

rubrics_metrics.name: "Is This a Story?" Test
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporters mentally assess whether the release constitutes a journalistic story rather than mere promotion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checks include: Is there an angle here that's not just promotional? Can I verify the claims? Will my editor approve? Does this fit our publication's voice? Have we covered this exact topic recently? The release should present verifiable, editorially defensible angles that align with the outlet and beat.

rubrics_metrics.name: What Increases Coverage Probability
rubrics_metrics.description: Tactics or features of distribution and content that measurably raise the chance a journalist will cover the release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples and reported multipliers: personal email vs. wire distribution (10x increase); offering an exclusive (3x increase); embargo with notice (2x increase, if the reporter is trusted); providing pre-built data visualizations (1.5x increase); reporter has covered the company before (2x increase). Use personalization, exclusives, useful assets, and relationships to improve pickup.

rubrics_metrics.name: What Decreases Coverage Probability
rubrics_metrics.description: Timing, language, and formatting choices that push releases to the bottom of the pile or cause deletion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid sending during a major news event (anything global pushes you to the bottom); avoid Friday afternoon sends; do not use hyperbolic subject-line words like "groundbreaking" or "revolutionary"; do not make boilerplate longer than the actual news; avoid quotes attributed to the PR firm; and avoid visible multiple bcc/cc'd recipients. These are common triggers for dismissal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editor's Filter (Second Stage)
rubrics_metrics.description: After a reporter is interested, editors evaluate whether the story should run.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors judge: audience interest; newsworthiness vs. promotional balance; differentiation from existing coverage; SEO opportunity; and visual story potential. Releases should meet editorial priorities and demonstrate clear value to the outlet's audience and metrics (e.g., SEO, visuals).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Rubric From Journalists' Side
rubrics_metrics.description: A concise checklist of qualities journalists say a good press release should have.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subject line accurate and specific; newsworthy beyond promotional value; story angle visible immediately; source verifiable; multimedia ready; timing strategic; personalized to beat. Use this checklist to evaluate your release before sending.
